solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Flamboyant lawyers love what Manuel says (7)

indicatorNotes.what Manuel says: Manuel speaks Spanish, so the phrase asks for the Spanish word he would say for 'what'

blocks.note: love = nil = O, from tennis scoring

annotation.surface: A showy legal team and a bewildered waiter.
annotation.walkthrough: Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, whose catchphrase is a baffled '¿Qué?'.
annotation.definitionFit: The ornate seventeenth-century style of art and music gives its name to anything extravagantly showy.

entries.clue: Make pale line in the sand (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the line inside the sand, so one piece sits within the other

annotation.surface: Someone draws a line in the sand and loses their nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line in the sand' is a stock phrase for a limit, so it reads as one idea; split it, and the line goes inside the beach.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chemically whitening cloth or hair takes the colour out of it.

entries.clue: Try splitting beam of light up in practice (9)

indicatorNotes.splitting: to split something is to come between its parts, so the first piece sits inside the second
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' turns the letters to read bottom to top

blocks.note: a laser is a beam of light
a judge will try, or hear, a case

annotation.surface: An experiment splitting a light beam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but it is the courtroom sense: to hear a case.
annotation.definitionFit: Actors run through a play before opening night; that run-through is practice.

entries.clue: Case of Ecuadorians occupying capital? Yes (5,2)

indicatorNotes.Case of: a case is the outside of a thing, so the word's first and last letters
indicatorNotes.occupying: to occupy a city is to be inside it, so the letters sit within the capital

blocks.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador

annotation.surface: A question about Ecuadorians living in their own capital.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital is Ecuador's own, which is what makes the surface hang together.
annotation.definitionFit: A rather formal British phrase of agreement, said where others would say yes.

entries.clue: Fresh lime in tea to remove, maybe from the cup (9)

indicatorNotes.Fresh: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: Fishing a slice of lime out of a cup of tea.
annotation.walkthrough: The cup is a trophy, not a teacup: teams are knocked out of a cup competition.
annotation.definitionFit: A knocked-out team is removed from the cup, a sporting sense 'maybe' flags as one example.

entries.clue: Issue pound, having gained backing, more or less (7)

indicatorNotes.having gained: the pound has something added, so the next piece comes after it
indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so the assembled pair is turned back to front

annotation.surface: A currency story: sterling gains support and is roughly stable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is the verb, not a problem: to put out a book or statement.
annotation.definitionFit: A publisher issues books and papers; as verbs the two are straight synonyms.

entries.clue: One’s balance improves certainly during gymnastics lesson (5)

annotation.definitionNote: a clause standing for 'one whose balance improves'

indicatorNotes.during: during means within a span of time, so the word goes within the lesson

blocks.note: PE = physical education, a school gym class

annotation.surface: A pupil's balance gets better in gym class.
annotation.walkthrough: The gymnast's balance is a bank balance: the person being paid sees their account go up.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: whoever receives a payment finds their bank balance improves.

entries.clue: Area trading with rubles (7)

indicatorNotes.trading: to trade is to exchange, so the letters exchange places

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: this is a country that does its trading in rubles.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: this Eastern European state's currency is the Belarusian ruble.

entries.clue: Mad assessor’s self-explanatory statement? (5)

blocks.note: an assessor's job is rating, so his description of it is a two-word sentence

annotation.surface: An angry assessor explains himself.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I RATE and it is an assessor describing his own job; the question mark flags the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry, and a two-word sentence an assessor might say of himself.

entries.clue: Doubt that boy will chase mates out of bounds (8)

indicatorNotes.out of bounds: a word's bounds are its first and last letters, and those are put out

blocks.note: in the game of tag, whoever is 'it' does the chasing
mATEs without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A schoolboy chasing his friends out of the playground.
annotation.walkthrough: The playground game is the key: the one who chases is 'it', so 'that boy will chase' is HE'S IT.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to be unsure and waver before acting.

entries.clue: Roots tangled in the densely packed place (9)

indicatorNotes.tangled: tangled things are twisted out of order, as the letters are

blocks.note: a city is a crowded place

annotation.surface: Tree roots tangled under a crowded city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roots' sounds botanical, but it means where a person's family comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Your roots are your ancestral and cultural origins, the group you descend from.

entries.clue: See a police officer gets a round in, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: lo = see!, as in 'lo and behold'

annotation.surface: A police officer buying a round of drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The round is a bullet, not drinks: putting a cartridge in a gun is getting a round in.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: putting a cartridge into a gun is one way of charging it, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Have a hankering for chicken, mostly (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: chicken = cowardly, a six-letter synonym; 'mostly' drops its final N

annotation.surface: Someone longing for chicken.
annotation.walkthrough: Chicken is the adjective, cowardly, not something to eat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to long for or yearn for something.

entries.clue: Really not far from home on island (2,7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so 'not far from home' comes after the island

annotation.surface: Living close to home on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Really' is the adverb, as in 'she meant it really', not an exclamation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: meant seriously, sincerely, not as a joke.

entries.clue: In photo, auntie thanks new salesperson (4,9)

indicatorNotes.In: 'In photo' means inside the photo, so the following pieces go within it

blocks.note: an aunt is Pa's sis, father's sister

annotation.surface: An aunt in a photo thanks a new sales assistant.
annotation.walkthrough: The leap is that an aunt can be described rather than named: your father's sister, written as a possessive and an abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who serves customers behind a shop counter.

entries.clue: Holding broken TV, consult office’s tech whizz (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Holding: to hold is to have inside, so the outer word holds the other letters
indicatorNotes.broken: broken into pieces, so T and V are separated and placed apart

blocks.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
an office is a job; JOB'S

annotation.surface: Calling the office tech expert about a broken television.
annotation.walkthrough: The T and V go into SEE separately, one after each of its first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Apple co-founder is the best-known technology visionary of his era.

entries.clue: Equally cold final section on the way up (9)

blocks.note: an ending is the final part

annotation.surface: A climb whose last stretch is just as cold.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a mountaineer's report, which keeps 'on the way up' looking like description rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rising or climbing.

entries.clue: Game in which king swaps letter, initially for a D (8)

indicatorNotes.swaps: to swap is to give one thing up in exchange, so the king gives up a letter
indicatorNotes.for: 'for' means in exchange for, so the new letters take the old one's place

blocks.note: used as is, replacing the L

annotation.surface: A word game with a king changing letters.
annotation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the game itself is one of acting out words syllable by syllable.
annotation.definitionFit: A party game in which players mime a word or title for others to guess.

entries.clue: Poet whose children were naughty smearing earlobe with chilli (7,6)

indicatorNotes.smearing: smearing spreads and mixes things, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: Naughty children rubbing chilli on someone's earlobe.
annotation.walkthrough: The poet wrote Cautionary Tales for Children, verses in which badly behaved children come to grisly ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by his best-known work: his comic verses are all about badly behaved children.

entries.clue: Knock top off pot taken by gambler? (7)

indicatorNotes.top off: in a down clue, the top is the first letter, and it comes off

blocks.note: a gambler's take is his winnings; drop the W

annotation.surface: A gambler knocking over a pot.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman's turn at the crease is called a knock.
annotation.definitionFit: Cricket slang: a batsman's knock is his turn at batting.

entries.clue: Well grounded soldier enters the nearest pub (7)

indicatorNotes.enters: to enter a pub is to go inside it, so the soldier's letters go inside the pub's

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub
a GI is an American soldier

annotation.surface: A sensible soldier walks into the local.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well grounded' looks like a description of the soldier, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An argument with sound grounds follows reason, so it is rational.

entries.clue: Rush someone who minds taking drug (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: to take a drug is to take it in, so the drug goes inside the carer

annotation.surface: Hurrying a carer who has taken drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush' is a verb here: the answer is not a job but hurtling out of control.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb, to hurtle along at speed, often out of control.

entries.clue: Talk of the old days, short skirts in the playground back in style? (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in the playground' puts the skirts inside the playground's letters
indicatorNotes.back in: the back of a word is its end, so its last letter

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground

annotation.surface: Nostalgia for miniskirts in the playground and whether they'll return to fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back in style' reads as a fashion revival; it is the last letter of 'style'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to recall past times fondly, usually out loud with others.

entries.clue: Singer joined then given audition (5)

indicatorNotes.given audition: an audition is literally a hearing, so the pieces are heard, not read

annotation.surface: A singer who joined a company after an audition.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian double Z is said 'ts', so the word sounds like MET SO.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for mezzo-soprano, a female voice between soprano and contralto.

entries.clue: Quality of drink that’s uncertain (5)

blocks.note: er is a sound of hesitation

annotation.surface: Someone unsure how good a drink is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quality' is the adjective, as in 'quality goods', not the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal adjectives for first-rate, as in 'a quality meal'.

entries.clue: Sail boatbuilder shortened after trimming edges for ages (5)

indicatorNotes.shortened: a shortened word is cut short, so it loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.after: the boatbuilder comes after the trimmed ages in the answer
indicatorNotes.trimming edges: trimming cuts off edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: NOAH, builder of the Ark, without his last letter

annotation.surface: A sailmaker trimming a boatbuilder's work.
annotation.walkthrough: The boatbuilder is the biblical one who built the Ark.
annotation.definitionFit: A large jib that overlaps the mainsail, named after the Italian port.

entries.clue: Nap before noon having so many hours until then (5)

annotation.surface: A morning nap with hours to go before lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Then' is noon: counting from midnight, twelve hours pass until it.
annotation.definitionFit: Twelve hours run from midnight to noon, and twelve is the number meant.

entries.clue: Ban plagiarism in written work (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in written work' puts the plagiarism inside the written work's letters

blocks.note: to crib is to copy another's work

annotation.surface: A ban on copying in essays.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a school rule on copying, which hides the verb 'ban' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to forbid or outlaw officially.

entries.clue: Sopranos cast short of a godfather? (7)

indicatorNotes.cast: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order
indicatorNotes.short of: short of means lacking, so the word goes without the A

annotation.surface: The cast of The Sopranos, the mafia TV drama, missing its godfather.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mafia godfather is a red herring: the other kind stands for a child at baptism.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a godparent formally vouches for a child at baptism, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Classic sandcastle — Geraldine holds with symmetry (2,5)

indicatorNotes.holds: to hold is to contain, so the phrase contains the answer
indicatorNotes.with symmetry: symmetry means equal on both sides, so the answer sits dead centre, six letters either side

annotation.surface: Geraldine building a perfectly symmetrical sandcastle.
annotation.walkthrough: The hidden word sits exactly in the middle of the two words, which is what 'with symmetry' promises.
annotation.definitionFit: Racing's five Classics are the major British flat races, and this Doncaster race is the oldest.
